key_insight: Geometric, semi-analytical synthesis produces smooth, robust single-qubit controls in tens of milliseconds rather than minutes.
engineering_relevance: Faster dynamically corrected gate synthesis could reduce control-design overhead while preserving high fidelity and resilience to quasistatic amplitude and dephasing errors.
method: Map quantum evolution to space curves using Space Curve Quantum Control and a Frenet–Serret frame.
Apply the Pontryagin Maximum Principle, solve the boundary-value problem by shooting, and integrate frames with Rodrigues’ formula.
Build a reference-solution library across rotation angles and interpolate initial guesses for new gates.
evidence_signal: Across 2,000 single-qubit rotations, mean local optimization took 39.945 ms per gate after interpolation-base preparation; quantum propagation showed nominal infidelities below 10^-9 after virtual phase correction and verified quasistatic-error robustness.
watch_item: Reported timings exclude interpolation-base preparation, and performance under hardware constraints or time-varying noise remains to be established.
paper_title: Semi-Analytical Geometric Synthesis of Robust Quantum Controls
